chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Fadl, who said: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Farazdaq informed me, who said: Ali ibn Musa ibn al-Ahwal narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Abi al-Sari narrated to me orally, who said: Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Balawi narrated to us, who said: Amara ibn Zayd narrated from Abu Amir al-Saji, the preacher of the people of Hijaz, who said:

I came to Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) and said to him: O son of the Messenger of God, what is the reward for one who visits his grave, meaning the Commander of the Faithful, and frequents his soil?

He said: O Abu Amir, my father narrated to me from his father from his grandfather Al-Husayn ibn Ali, from Ali (peace be upon him), that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'By God, you will surely be killed in the land of Iraq and buried in it.'

I said: O Messenger of God, what is the reward for one who visits our graves and frequents them and maintains them? He said to me: O Abu al-Hasan, indeed God has made your grave and the grave of your children a valley among the valleys of Paradise and a courtyard among its courtyards.

And indeed God has made the hearts of the elite of His creation and the choicest of His servants yearn for you and endure humiliation and hardship for your sake, so they frequent your graves and increase their visits to them, seeking closeness to God and love for the Messenger of God from among them.
Those are the ones, O Ali, who are specially granted my intercession and are the ones who will drink from my basin, and they are my visitors tomorrow in Paradise.
O Ali, whoever frequents your graves and maintains them is as if he helped Sulayman ibn Dawud in building the Holy House.
And whoever visits your graves, the equivalent of that is for him the reward of seventy pilgrimages after the pilgrimage of Islam.
And his sins are removed until he returns from your visitation as he was on the day his mother gave birth to him.
So rejoice and give glad tidings to your friends and lovers of the bliss and delight of the eye, of what no eye has seen and no ear has heard and no heart of a human has conceived.
But a remnant of the people reproach the visitors of your graves for visiting you, just as the adulteress is reproached for her adultery.
Those are the worst of my Ummah; my intercession will not reach them and they will not drink from my basin.

key_terms.قُبُورَنَا: Our graves (referring to the Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting the graves of the Imams according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the theological significance of *Ziyarat* (visitation) as an act of devotion to the Ahl al-Bayt, linking the physical act of visiting graves to spiritual purification and eschatological reward. Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) highlights that maintaining these graves invites divine love and grants the visitor the Prophet's intercession (*Shafa'ah*) and entry from his Basin (*Hawd*), while contrasting true believers with those who mock such practices. The narrative underscores the continuity of prophetic tradition, tracing the promise of Ali's martyrdom in Iraq back to the Prophet himself, thereby validating the sanctity of the Iraqi shrines in Shia piety.
